figures.caption: Table 1: Comparison of different methods on NIH-PAN and MSD-PAN datasets demonstrating the advantages of our method. Results are reported as mean±std. Best results are in red, second-best in blue.

Fig. 1: (a) Limited supervision signals on morphologically diverse pancreas data lead to Supervision Bias. (b) Existing methods suffer from poor generalizability, due to the lack of shared structural knowledge across samples. (c) SCKAN proposes the first cross-sample structural consensus learning with KANs to capture shared knowledge, enhancing generalizability.

Fig. 3: 2D slice, 3D visualizations and metric performance on 5% NIH-PAN dataset illustrating our method’s capability in preserving structural completeness and achieving accurate segmentation without extra predictions.

Fig. 2: (a) SCKAN achieves generalizable and accurate SSPS results, consisting of (b) SPCL promoting unbiased structural representation and (c) CKaF reducing morphology-specific bias via aggregating consensus.
